From: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>
Date: Fri, Dec 5, 2014 at 12:46 PM
Subject: Re: BioGeoBEARS - Stochastic mapping
To: xxx

Hi!  Glad it's working mostly at least -- I still haven't had time to make it a package yet.

Two things to try:

1. Make sure you do:

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

...at the beginning of your script every time you run it

2. It looks like you are hitting the "maxtries" limit. This means that, for a particular branch, the simulation of history along that branch is having a problem getting from the simulated ancestor to the simulated descendant. This can happen e.g. if you have some very "unlucky" draws for ancestor/descendant, and/or a data configuration which is very unlikely under the model.

Solutions:
2a. Increase maxtries by 10 or 100 times (may slow down the simulation somewhat)
2b. Try a different random number seed

Some of this is in the error message, I'll try to make that more detailed when I revise it.

It looks like it's running sometimes, so probably you just need to increase maxtries.

Cheers,
Nick

PS: I'll add you to BioGeoBEARS...

This question (anonymized) was caused by having a root edge on a tree being used in a stratified analysis. I've now added a automatic check to remove root edges from stratified analyses.

Thanks for the question!

Cheers,
Nick

To: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>

Hi -- nevermind, I figured it out.  What was screwing it up was the root branch in your phylogeny, which created an extra edge in the list of edges, which screwed up the indexing of edges.

The attached tree works...

I've added a fix to the stratified code to automatically remove the root branch.  Thanks for the note!

Cheers!
Nick

messages.subject_clean: state/range probabilities at each node in BioGeoBEARS
messages.body_plain:
Answer about getting the probabilities of each state (each geographic range) at each node..

Cheers!
Nick

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>
Date: Wed, Dec 17, 2014 at 2:24 PM
Subject: Re: BioGeoBEARS outputs
To: Lukas Ruber <lukas...@nmbe.ch>

Hi!  Thanks for the question.

Yes, it's even easier than Lagrange to get the probabilities of each ancestral state. E.g. if the result object is "res", they are stored in the listed elements in "res":

names(res)

E.g. the probabilities of each states at each node are in:

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node

The probabilities of each state at each "corner" (branch bottom, representing the states instantaneously after cladogenesis splits) are in:

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node

These tables have:

rows: tips, then root node, then internal nodes -- numbered as in the APE package defaults or the prt() function

columns: states (each state is a geographic range, e.g. for 2 areas there are 4 states/ranges: null, A, B, or AB

See e.g.: http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#node_numbering

Note that these are the state probabilities under the global ML model. Lagrange does state probabilities slightly differently, by fixing each ancestral state at each node and re-optimizing the model parameters under each constraint. They are typically similar but there can be some differences. See Matzke 2014, Sys Bio.

Cheers!  Hope it works for you, let me know how it goes.

Nick

PS: Can I post this answer to the BioGeoBEARS google group?  It will help other people...
